<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document is the contract for the resource bounds pcrec and an emitted matcher enforce: the numbers, the flags that move them, and what a caller observes when one is crossed. The code space of the give-up codes and the rules of their propagation are `docs/spec/match_api.md` §4; this document states the numbers and does not restate those rules. Every default below is a row of `src/core/limits.def`, which `pcrec --list-limits` prints (§3.4a); the sections named in that listing's `anchor` column are §3.1-§3.9 and §8, and `tests/registry/limits_check.sh` checks each anchored value against its section's text. The history of these bounds is `docs/dev/history/limits_record.md`, which is not normative.

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. Scope of the guarantee

<a id="s1-p1"></a>[1¶1] pcrec is an ahead-of-time compiler run over patterns the caller controls. Hardening the engine against a deliberately adversarial pattern is out of scope. The guarantee is narrower and unconditional: a give-up is never a false answer.

<a id="s1-p2"></a>[1¶2] Every give-up code is a negative return strictly below `-1`, distinct from a match (`>= 0`) and from a clean no-match (`-1`), and `caps`/`caps_out` are untouched on every one (`match_api.md` §4). A caller that reaches a bound gets "unknown", never a wrong match or a wrong span.

<a id="s1-p3"></a>[1¶3] A bound on compile TIME is not part of the contract (§3.3.5, §7).

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. The give-up codes

| code | value | fires when |
|---|---|---|
| `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` | `-2` | the step budget (§3.1) is exhausted |
| `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` | `-3` | the resume stack or its trail (§3.2) is exhausted; the code names the resource, not which of the two arrays ran out |
| `PCREC_ERR_WORK` | `-4` | the work budget (§3.1) is exhausted |
| `PCREC_ERR_RECURSE` | `-5`, equal to `PCREC_ERR_FLOOR` | reserved; no artifact returns it |

<a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] `PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL` (`-6`) lies below `PCREC_ERR_FLOOR` and is not a give-up; it reports the artifact detecting its own inconsistency (`match_api.md` §4). Which entries can return which code, the obligation on composed call sites to trap below the floor, and why a DFA artifact emits these constants without returning them are `match_api.md` §4.

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. The numbers

<a id="s3-1"></a>
### 3.1 Step and work budgets

<a id="s3-1-p1"></a>[3.1¶1] The step budget defaults to 500,000,000 (`VM_DEFAULT_STEP_BUDGET`). It is substituted whenever `pcrec_options.step_budget` holds its sentinel `PCREC_STEP_BUDGET_DEFAULT`, and `--step-budget=N` sets it per compile. It counts backtrack resumptions; forward progress is free. It is a robustness bound, not a latency guarantee.

<a id="s3-1-p2"></a>[3.1¶2] The work budget defaults to 1,000,000,000 (`VM_DEFAULT_WORK_BUDGET`), substituted from `PCREC_WORK_BUDGET_DEFAULT`, and `--work-budget=N` sets it. It is a separate counter: one unit per forward-only operation the fail label does not see (a frame discarded at a cut, a frameless scan iteration).

<a id="s3-1-p3"></a>[3.1¶3] `--fno-step-budget` emits neither counter; one gate covers both. `rx_info.step_budget` and `rx_info.work_budget` carry the enforced values, `-1` when disabled.

<a id="s3-1-p4"></a>[3.1¶4] A run of three or more consecutive literal bytes is compared as one constant-length `memcmp` (`tuning.md` §2.31) and charged as ONE compare; a two-byte run stays a byte chain. A run that mismatches at any byte enters the fail label once, so the step count of every match attempt equals what the per-byte chain charged. In a concatenation the work budget is unchanged. In an alternation island a walk that dies charges the trie bytes proved before the failing compare, never the bytes the one compare examined, so a `PCREC_ERR_WORK` give-up can only move later. The compile-time node budget `PCREC_MAX_VM_NODES` still pays one node per literal byte.

<a id="s3-2"></a>
### 3.2 Frame and trail capacities

<a id="s3-2-p1"></a>[3.2¶1] The resume stack defaults to 2,048 frames and the trail to 3,072 entries (`VM_DEFAULT_RESUME_FRAMES`, `VM_DEFAULT_TRAIL_FRAMES`). They are emitted as `<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES`/`<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES` and mirrored as `rx_info.resume_frames`/`trail_frames` (`match_api.md` §10.4). `--backtrack-frames=N` sets the compiled-in capacity per artifact; where the pattern's depth is statically bounded the emitter sizes the capacity exactly, clamped at `VM_MAX_AUTO_RESUME_FRAMES`/`VM_MAX_AUTO_TRAIL_FRAMES` (2,048 and 3,072). Both capacities are `0` on a DFA artifact, so a caller must check before dividing by either macro.

<a id="s3-2-p2"></a>[3.2¶2] The run struct these capacities size lives on a stack frame, which is why the defaults are not larger (§5). The caller-provided buffer (`match_api.md` §10) is the route past the ceiling.

<a id="s3-2-p3"></a>[3.2¶3] The un-suffixed entries (`<prefix>_search`, `_match`, `_match_caps`) reach the capacities in two steps where the stamped default does not fit one 4 KB page: they run first on a small page-budgeted buffer (`<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES`/`<PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL`, `match_api.md` §6.3) and escalate to the full stamped default on a `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` give-up and on nothing else, re-running the match from scratch with both budgets refilled (`match_api.md` §10.9). The depth an artifact reaches and every answer it gives are identical with and without the tier; a give-up always means the stamped default ran out. `-fno-tiered-entry` (`tuning.md` §2.12) removes the tier.

<a id="s3-2-p4"></a>[3.2¶4] The tier is a bet and its losing case is a limit. The wasted fast attempt is bounded by the step and work budgets, not by the fast frame count, so an escalating call can spend up to twice §3.1's step budget before it answers. The transition is a cliff: below the depth where a pattern's backtracking exhausts the fast buffer the call is much cheaper than single-tier, above it somewhat dearer. The boundary is a property of the pattern's backtracking depth, not of the input length. A workload that sits above its patterns' boundaries should use the `_in` entries or `-fno-tiered-entry`.

<a id="s3-3"></a>
### 3.3 Compile-time budgets

<a id="s3-3-1"></a>
#### 3.3.1 The hard ceilings

<a id="s3-3-1-p1"></a>[3.3.1¶1] Six state-count ceilings in `src/core/limits.h` are a promise: crossing one makes the compile FAIL cleanly, naming the ceiling, never hang, exhaust memory or truncate.

| ceiling | default | bounds |
|---|---|---|
| `PCREC_MAX_NFA_STATES` | 131,072 | NFA states |
| `PCREC_MAX_VM_NODES` | 131,072 | VM program nodes |
| `PCREC_MAX_DFA_STATES_GOTO` | 10,000 | the computed-goto DFA engine |
| `PCREC_MAX_DFA_STATES_TABLE` | 32,000 | the table DFA engine |
| `PCREC_MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES` | 2,000,000 | the states-times-classes transition table |
| `PCREC_MAX_SUBSET_ELEMS` | 48,000,000 | the element total of the priority subset construction |

<a id="s3-3-1-p2"></a>[3.3.1¶2] `pcrec --list-limits` reproduces every number (§3.4a).

<a id="s3-3-2"></a>
#### 3.3.2 The raise-only overrides

<a id="s3-3-2-p1"></a>[3.3.2¶1] `--max-nfa-states=N`, `--max-dfa-states-goto=N` and `--max-subset-elems=N` raise the matching ceiling per compile; `--max-auto-dfa-elems=N` raises the auto-route budget (§3.3.4); `--max-emit-code-bytes=N` and `--max-emit-bytes=N` raise the size caps (§8.6). A value below the built-in default is refused as a malformed option, so an override can never manufacture a refusal. The library members are `max_nfa_states`, `max_dfa_states_goto`, `max_subset_elems`, `max_auto_dfa_elems`, `max_emit_code_bytes`, `max_emit_bytes` of `pcrec_options`; `0` means the built-in default.

<a id="s3-3-2-p2"></a>[3.3.2¶2] `PCREC_MAX_DFA_STATES_TABLE`, `PCREC_MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES` and `PCREC_MAX_VM_NODES` have no override. The table engine's transition cell is a 16-bit integer (the premultiplied form reserves 65,535 as its dead sentinel), so 32,000 states already sits just under what the cell can represent; raising the ceiling needs a wider cell type, which is an `abi` event.

<a id="s3-3-3"></a>
#### 3.3.3 The DFA-side exceptions

<a id="s3-3-3-p1"></a>[3.3.3¶1] Under `--engine=auto`, crossing `PCREC_MAX_DFA_STATES_TABLE`, `PCREC_MAX_DFA_STATES_GOTO`, `PCREC_MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES` or `PCREC_MAX_SUBSET_ELEMS` fails the DFA build with the same diagnostic and cost, but the compile does not necessarily fail: the overflow is a selection outcome (fall back to the VM; drop an auto-selected prefilter), so a pattern may succeed on the VM. `PCREC_MAX_NFA_STATES` and `PCREC_MAX_VM_NODES` have no fallback engine and keep the ceiling unconditionally, and `--engine=dfa` and `-fprefilter` keep it for all six (`tuning.md` §2.11 states the mechanism and its cost bound).

<a id="s3-3-3-p2"></a>[3.3.3¶2] A DFA artifact may carry an optional third machine, the anchored match-here automaton behind `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped"` (`tuning.md` §2.15). It is built after the two mandatory machines and charged against the same three DFA-side ceilings; crossing one produces no diagnostic and no fallback engine, and the artifact keeps the search-and-filter form and stamps it. The optional machine's bytes also count toward the emitted-size caps (§8); the driver drops it and re-emits before a size cap refuses (§8.4), so an optional machine never decides which patterns pcrec accepts, in either unit.

<a id="s3-3-4"></a>
#### 3.3.4 The auto-route budget and the prefilter retry

<a id="s3-3-4-p1"></a>[3.3.4¶1] `PCREC_MAX_AUTO_DFA_ELEMS` (30,000,000) is a smaller budget on the same running count as `PCREC_MAX_SUBSET_ELEMS`, checked at the same site, only under `--engine=auto`, and only against the two mandatory machines. Crossing it abandons the DFA attempt and falls back to the VM through the same mechanism as §3.3.3, and writes one stderr line naming the limit and `--max-auto-dfa-elems`. `--engine=dfa` is unaffected and pays the full `PCREC_MAX_SUBSET_ELEMS`.

<a id="s3-3-4-p2"></a>[3.3.4¶2] When an emitted-size cap refuses an artifact, the driver makes one more attempt with the VM hybrid's prefilter built from the count-collapsed language (`tuning.md` §2.17) and refuses only if that is over the caps too. No pattern that compiles stops compiling because of it. The retry adds attempts, never headroom: nothing is emitted past a cap, and a pattern is refused unless some attempt produces an artifact under it. `-fno-prefilter-collapse` denies it; the ladder's next row then drops the prefilter instead (§8.4). The retry never applies where the DFA is the engine, where the language must be exact, and it ships no prefilter where the collapsed language is nullable (`tuning.md` §2.17 carries the rule, the stamps and the flag interactions).

<a id="s3-3-5"></a>
#### 3.3.5 What is not promised

<a id="s3-3-5-p1"></a>[3.3.5¶1] pcrec makes no promise about wall-clock compile time for an accepted pattern. The state-count ceilings and the size caps (§8) are the only compile-side bounds a caller can rely on.

<a id="s3-4"></a>
### 3.4 The buffer sizing surface

<a id="s3-4-p1"></a>[3.4¶1] A caller sizing a caller-provided buffer reads the macros and `rx_info` fields in `match_api.md` §10.4, which states the arithmetic, including the rule that a stamped size `0` means the engine takes no buffers.

<a id="s3-4a"></a>
### 3.4a Reading a limit from a program: `pcrec_limits_tsv`

<a id="s3-4a-p1"></a>[3.4a¶1] The public header declares:

```c
char *pcrec_limits_tsv(void);   /* lib/pcrec.h; caller frees with free() */
```

<a id="s3-4a-p2"></a>[3.4a¶2] It renders `src/core/limits.def`, the single home of every numeric limit, as one TSV in the wire format of `table_contract.md`, and is the same table `pcrec --list-limits` prints. It returns NULL on allocation failure. The header row is `#name value unit kind override anchor desc`, tab-separated.

<a id="s3-4a-p3"></a>[3.4a¶3] The `override` column says how a caller moves the number. `flag` means a CLI flag or `pcrec_options` field moves it per compile. `-D` means only pcrec's own build does. `flag+-D` means a caller flag moves it per compile and a build-time `-D` moves the built-in default that flag's floor is measured against. `none` means nothing does.

<a id="s3-4a-p4"></a>[3.4a¶4] The `unit` column says how to read `value`: a count of a thing (`bytes`, `states`, `positions`), `percent` (a fraction of another row's quantity), or `bits` (information: `PCREC_MIN_REQ_RUN_BITS` is a sum of `popcount(K)` over a run's positions, `tuning.md` §2.28). Selection knees carry no anchor in this document (§8b); `tuning.md` §2.20 states the rule and §2.39 the required-run knees.

<a id="s3-4a-p5"></a>[3.4a¶5] No limit is duplicated into `lib/pcrec.h` as a macro: a second spelling could drift from `limits.def`. The six `max_*` members of `pcrec_options` are raise-only (§3.3.2), so a caller raising one reads its default from this function.

<a id="s3-5"></a>
### 3.5 The `.rxt` source parser's caps

<a id="s3-5-p1"></a>[3.5¶1] `pcrec --list-source`, and the compile of a `.rxt` source file, parse the file head with these fixed caps:

- <a id="s3-5-p2"></a>[3.5¶2] A `config` name, a `target` prefix and a `target` definition name are each at most 127 bytes. Crossing it reports a diagnostic that names the cap (for example `'config' name is too long (N bytes, max 127)`), not the "needs a name" message a missing name gets. A `with`/`from` list element has no cap of its own.
- <a id="s3-5-p3"></a>[3.5¶3] `config … from` nests at most 64 deep before it is refused, naming the construct.
- <a id="s3-5-p4"></a>[3.5¶4] The whole file is read into memory with no size cap; a source file is authored, not received from an untrusted caller.
- <a id="s3-5-p5"></a>[3.5¶5] `pcrec_error.msg` is 256 bytes. The diagnostic's `file:line:` prefix is composed first, so a long sentence truncates in the direction that keeps the file and line.

<a id="s3-6"></a>
### 3.6 Module `vars`: the expansion grammar's caps

<a id="s3-6-p1"></a>[3.6¶1] Module `vars` (`vars.md`) gives a pattern the expansion `${ [!] name [ operator word ] }`. Two numbers bound its spelling, both at compile time, both refusing the pattern by name when crossed; neither is movable by a flag.

- <a id="s3-6-p2"></a>[3.6¶2] A variable name is at most `PCREC_MAX_VAR_NAME_LEN` = 64 bytes. The name is emitted into an internal index macro's identifier and into the artifact's variable-names table (`rx_info.vars`), the same reason `-p` is bounded by `PCREC_MAX_PREFIX_LEN`. Nothing truncates.
- <a id="s3-6-p3"></a>[3.6¶3] An operator's word may nest further `${...}` expansions at most `PCREC_MAX_VAR_NEST_DEPTH` = 8 levels deep. Nesting is permitted in the word position only; the outermost reference is depth 0. The bound is a compile-time one and the emitted matcher gains no run-time recursion.

<a id="s3-7"></a>
### 3.7 Findings data

<a id="s3-7-p1"></a>[3.7¶1] An analysis's data blocks store counts, which the compiler turns into rates (`findings.md`). These bounds apply; each refusal names the limit and nothing truncates; none is movable by a flag.

- <a id="s3-7-p2"></a>[3.7¶2] A `row` count is at most `PCREC_MAX_FIND_COUNT` = 1,099,511,627,776 (2^40), which keeps the normalization's product inside 64-bit integers so rates are bit-identical on every box.
- <a id="s3-7-p3"></a>[3.7¶3] Every byte's rate is at least `PCREC_FIND_FLOOR_PPM` = 2 parts per million; a byte a block never counted is given the floor, so no reader treats a byte as impossible.
- <a id="s3-7-p4"></a>[3.7¶4] An analysis chain holds at most `PCREC_MAX_FIND_CHAIN` = 8 links before its built-in `default` terminal (the selected bundle and each `include` it follows).
- <a id="s3-7-p5"></a>[3.7¶5] An analysis text is at most `PCREC_MAX_FIND_BUNDLE_BYTES` = 1,048,576 bytes (an `-I DIR/<name>.rxt` file or a library caller's `analysis_source`); a larger one is refused before it is parsed.
- <a id="s3-7-p6"></a>[3.7¶6] A `cpfreq` block carries at most `PCREC_MAX_FIND_CPFREQ_ROWS` = 65,536 `row` lines. With `PCREC_MAX_FIND_COUNT` this keeps every derived byte count inside 64-bit integers; a block whose `encode-utf8`/`encode-latin1` derivation would put more than `PCREC_MAX_FIND_COUNT` on one byte is refused by that limit's name.

<a id="s3-8"></a>
### 3.8 Module `ucp`: which UCP sets compile

<a id="s3-8-p1"></a>[3.8¶1] Under `(*UCP)`/`--ucp` a class escape or POSIX class means a Unicode set (`cli.md` `--ucp`). A UCP set with more than `PCREC_UCP_NARROW_MAX_INTERVALS` = 128 code-point intervals, counted after clamping to the encoding's universe, is refused by name. Under `-e utf8` that is `\w \W` and `[:alpha:] [:alnum:] [:word:] [:lower:] [:upper:] [:graph:] [:print:] [:punct:]` at both polarities; `\d \D \s \S` and `[:digit:] [:xdigit:] [:space:] [:blank:] [:cntrl:]` compile. Under `-e byte` every set clamps far below 128 and all compile. Restricting the family (`(?aW)`, `(?aP)`) makes the construct ASCII and it compiles.

<a id="s3-8-p2"></a>[3.8¶2] This is a selection knee, not a resource ceiling, and is not movable by a flag. UCP `\b` and `\B` under `-e utf8` are refused by name with no number involved (the Unicode word set is not byte-expressible there); under `-e byte` they compile.

<a id="s3-9"></a>
### 3.9 The DFA's context sets and atoms

<a id="s3-9-p1"></a>[3.9¶1] A DFA machine tracks, for every context assertion it carries (`\b`/`\B`, a one-character lookaround turned context node, `(?m)^`/`(?m)$`, and under `-e utf8` the unanchored machine's character-boundary gate), which set the character on each side of a position is in. Two numbers bound it:

- <a id="s3-9-p2"></a>[3.9¶2] `PCREC_MAX_CTX_SETS` = 32 distinct context sets on one machine;
- <a id="s3-9-p3"></a>[3.9¶3] `PCREC_MAX_CTX_ATOMS` = 16 context atoms: the distinct membership vectors the machine's bytes realize over those sets, plus the empty one (an absent side).

<a id="s3-9-p4"></a>[3.9¶4] Over either, the DFA build is declined as a state-cap overflow is (§3.3.3): `--engine=auto` compiles the pattern on the VM, `--engine=dfa` refuses ("more than 16 context atoms on one machine; try --engine=vm"). A truncated partition is never produced. Neither is movable by a flag.

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. Worked example: `^(a(?1)?b)$`

<a id="s4-p1"></a>[4¶1] With `build/pcrec -p rx --features all --emit-main -o rec.c --pattern '^(a(?1)?b)$'` and the default capacities (§3.2), a subject of `n` `a` bytes followed by `n` `b` bytes matches for `n` up to 342 (a 684-byte subject) and returns `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` from `n` = 343 (686 bytes). `match_api.md` §10.1 states the same ceiling.

<a id="s4-p2"></a>[4¶2] The trail binds before the resume stack. The two arrays are sized by the stamped defaults (2,048 and 3,072), but this pattern's recursion costs about 2 resume frames and 9 trail entries per nesting level, so the 3,072-entry trail empties first with roughly two thirds of the resume stack unused. `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` is returned either way.

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. The default entries and the C stack

<a id="s5-p1"></a>[5¶1] The run struct behind the un-suffixed entries is sized by the capacities of §3.2. The entry itself runs on a page-sized buffer; the full-capacity struct is a local of a non-inlined internal function the entry calls only on a `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` give-up (`match_api.md` §10.9). So two stack quantities answer two questions, and `make test-stackdepth` prints both for the recursion specimen `^(a(?1)?b)$` built with `--engine=vm --features recursion`:

- <a id="s5-p2"></a>[5¶2] the entry's own frame stays under one 4 KB page (3,184 bytes for the specimen), which keeps gcc's stack-clash probing to one page per call;
- <a id="s5-p3"></a>[5¶3] the deep path, the entry's frame plus the internal function's (131,216 bytes), is what a call that escalates needs: 134,400 bytes for the specimen.

<a id="s5-p4"></a>[5¶4] The fit criterion is free stack headroom at the call site, not the thread's nominal stack size: the entry frame plus the deep path must fit in the headroom remaining where `<prefix>_search` is called. A thread's total size equals that headroom only at call depth zero. At depth zero a 131,072-byte (128 KB) thread is 3,328 bytes short of the specimen's 134,400, and an 8 MB thread is not.

<a id="s5-p5"></a>[5¶5] So the default entries are safe on a call site with at least the entry frame of headroom for every match the fast tier holds, and fault only on a subject deep enough to escalate. Which subjects escalate is a property of the pattern and the subject, so a caller cannot bound it in advance, and the deep tier's storage has no other legal home: a `static` fails the concurrency contract, a thread-local fails reentrancy, and allocation is forbidden by construction. This is `docs/dev/known_issues.md` K33.

<a id="s5-p6"></a>[5¶6] The remedy for the deep case is the caller-provided buffer (`match_api.md` §10): `<prefix>_search_in`'s own frame is 144 bytes for the specimen, and the 684-byte subject that kills the default entry on a 128 KB thread matches through `_search_in` on the same thread. It is the only way to a guarantee. A caller on a small-stack thread supplies its own frame and trail storage.

<a id="s6"></a>
## 6. Left recursion: a documented divergence

<a id="s6-p1"></a>[6¶1] On some same-position left recursions, for example `(a|(?1)a)b` on `"a"`, pcrec returns `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` where libpcre2 10.46 returns a clean no-match. A give-up asserts nothing about the language, so this is not a wrong answer, and it is not the general rule that same-position re-entry is always wrong: libpcre2's guard has five conjuncts, so a 199-deep same-position recursion can still match in both engines.

<a id="s6-p2"></a>[6¶2] pcrec does not adopt libpcre2's recursion-loop guard. Reproducing it needs a stored subject pointer per active recursion frame and a high-water mark threaded through every fail-and-return site of the emitted VM, on the hottest path, to reproduce one engine's implementation artefact. The give-up is pcrec's answer for this shape; the inverse divergence also exists (`((?1)?a)` on `"a"` matches here where libpcre2 reports its own error).

<a id="s6-p3"></a>[6¶3] The give-up is bounded by the same frame budget as every other recursive pattern (§3.2): a caller who needs the class to conclude has the same lever as any deep recursion, the `_in` entries with a larger buffer (§5).

<a id="s7"></a>
## 7. What is not limited

- <a id="s7-p1"></a>[7¶1] Compile time for an accepted pattern is not bounded. The state-count ceilings (§3.3) and the size caps (§8) bound quantities, not time: the code-bytes cap bounds the quantity that predicts compile time within one mechanism, but no emitted count is a compile-time oracle (a smaller artifact can take longer to compile than a larger one).
- <a id="s7-p2"></a>[7¶2] The size term can change a tuned caller's budget verdict. Choosing a different unroll factor `K` for the same pattern moves the give-up surface although it cannot move a match result: the minimum `--step-budget` that completes, the minimum `--backtrack-frames` (a smaller `K` raises the frame requirement) and `<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES` all change with `K`. Under the default budgets the answers are identical; a caller who has tuned a budget to the edge re-checks it after an emitter change that moves `K`, and `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K` shows which `K` the artifact got.
- <a id="s7-p3"></a>[7¶3] The step and work budgets are two counters, not an accounting of engine effort. No single number bounds total match time.
- <a id="s7-p4"></a>[7¶4] Possessification trades one counter for another. Any change to which loops `src/opt/possessify.c` marks (`-fno-possessify`, or a change to its verdict) moves a `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` or `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` give-up towards an answer and a `PCREC_ERR_WORK` give-up towards appearing: a possessive scan is charged to the work budget per iteration where the backtracking form spent steps on retreats (`tuning.md` §2.1). A caller who tuned `--work-budget` to the edge re-checks it after such a change; `<PREFIX>_VM_STRATS` shows whether the artifact carries a possessive loop.
- <a id="s7-p5"></a>[7¶5] `PCREC_ERR_RECURSE` is reserved and has no producer; there is no recursion-depth counter, so no number exists to state for it.

<a id="s8"></a>
## 8. Emitted artifact size

<a id="s8-1"></a>
### 8.1 The two limits

<a id="s8-1-p1"></a>[8.1¶1] pcrec bounds the size of the artifact it emits. Both limits are in bytes of emitted C source with comments excluded; the `.o` is roughly 17 % of that.

| limit | default | approx `.o` | bounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PCREC_MAX_VM_EMIT_CODE_BYTES` | 500,000 | 85 KB | bytes outside table initializers: the part gcc compiles as control flow |
| `PCREC_MAX_EMIT_BYTES` | 1,000,000 | 170 KB | the whole artifact |

<a id="s8-1-p2"></a>[8.1¶2] Both are checked after emission and before anything is written, so an over-limit compile produces a refusal and no file. They are emergency failsafes, not tuned thresholds: nothing in pcrec's corpus comes near either.

<a id="s8-1-p3"></a>[8.1¶3] Two limits exist because the size shipped and the cost gcc pays are different quantities. A data-table entry costs gcc about 0.9 µs, a computed-goto jump-table entry about 8.7 µs and a VM node about 5.4 ms, so a table-dominated artifact can be too large to ship yet cheap to compile (the total limit refuses it, the code limit does not), while a deeply nested bounded repeat can emit a modest size and cost gcc a minute (both refuse it when over). One limit would have to get one of those answers wrong.

<a id="s8-1-p4"></a>[8.1¶4] Comments are excluded from the measure, so `-fcomments`/`-fno-comments` (`tuning.md` §2.24) cannot rescue or refuse a pattern.

<a id="s8-2"></a>
### 8.2 Size limits and the prefix

<a id="s8-2-p1"></a>[8.2¶1] Every emitted length pcrec decides on is measured at a canonical prefix length of two bytes, whatever `-p` says. The artifact is emitted under a two-byte placeholder prefix and the caller's spelling is written onto the finished text last. So the two caps, the size term's trigger and ladder (§8a) and the VM entry-shape knee (`tuning.md` §2.21) read the artifact as it would be at `-p rx`, and the same pattern under the same options is accepted or refused, and takes the same forms, under every prefix.

<a id="s8-2-p2"></a>[8.2¶2] An artifact at a long prefix may therefore exceed a cap's number in real bytes, by up to `len(prefix) - 2` bytes per occurrence of the prefix; at the maximum prefix (`PCREC_MAX_PREFIX_LEN`, 60) that is under a third of the artifact. No stamp's value counts prefixed text: `<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES` counts at the canonical length. `tests/codegen/run_prefix_invariance.sh` checks this.

<a id="s8-3"></a>
### 8.3 Size limits and SIMD-guarded bytes

<a id="s8-3-p1"></a>[8.3¶1] Every emitted length pcrec decides on excludes the bytes the search-code kit writes under a CPU-level guard. A SIMD-on form (`-fmemfn-simd`, `tuning.md` §2.43) is its SIMD-off text plus whole guarded blocks (`#if <level>` … `#endif`), so subtracting those blocks gives the SIMD-off length exactly. The two caps, the size term's trigger, ladder and trial bound, and the VM entry-shape knee read that length, so turning SIMD on cannot rescue or refuse a pattern or move a ladder step, and every figure a refusal or a `--warn-emit-bytes` note quotes is the SIMD-off figure.

<a id="s8-3-p2"></a>[8.3¶2] At `-march=L` the guarded text is compiled, so an artifact may exceed a cap's number in compiled bytes by its guarded total, which `<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES` reports (`match_api.md` §6.3). There is no aggregate budget on it: each SIMD form bounds its own guarded bytes, and the stamped total is checked against the sum of those bounds. The stamp reads `0` on an artifact with no guarded block.

<a id="s8-3-p3"></a>[8.3¶3] At the default `-fno-memfn-simd` no artifact holds a guarded block, so the stamp reads `0` on every such artifact. At `-fmemfn-simd` it is nonzero exactly where a SIMD row rendered: the `vrun` rows (`registry.md` §6¶8a), over a FUNC whose predicate is one run. Such a FUNC's guarded bytes are at most 2,700 for `vrun-w16` and 2,800 for `vrun-w32`; `tests/memfn/simd_bounds.tsv` states each row's bound, measured over the kit's own generated site space.

<a id="s8-4"></a>
### 8.4 The size-cap ladder and `--size-cap=refuse`

<a id="s8-4-p1"></a>[8.4¶1] Before either limit refuses, pcrec tries a smaller form of the same artifact, one rung at a time. The rungs are one ordered table (`fit_rungs[]` in `src/core/compile.c`); the first row that applies to the refused artifact and is not denied is taken, and the compile re-emits. A rung applies only where its contributor exists. Every rung costs run time, never an answer.

| order | rung | engine | gives up | own deny |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `unroll-rescue`: a smaller unroll factor `K` picked to fit | VM | the unrolled counter copies | `-fno-size-term` (the whole term) |
| 2 | `prefilter-collapse`: the prefilter rebuilt from the count-collapsed language | VM hybrid | a filter that dismisses exactly the non-matching starts | `-fno-prefilter-collapse` |
| 3 | `drop-anchored`: the optional anchored match-here machine | DFA | `<prefix>_match`'s one-pass form | none |
| 4 | `drop-premul`: the premultiplied DFA transition table | DFA | one add per step | none |
| 5 | `drop-prefilter`: the VM hybrid's prefilter | VM hybrid | candidate skipping; the VM tries every start | none |

<a id="s8-4-p2"></a>[8.4¶2] The order is by measured cost, cheapest first, and the engine scope makes it bind only within one engine: rows 1, 2 and 5 are the VM's (row 1 runs inside every VM attempt, so before any retry), rows 3 and 4 the DFA's. Rungs 3 and 4 are tried in that order, either may fire, and both may fire on one artifact. Dropping the premultiplied table of a VM hybrid's embedded prefilter has no rung.

<a id="s8-4-p3"></a>[8.4¶3] `--size-cap=refuse` (`PCREC_SIZE_CAP_REFUSE`; `--size-cap=degrade` is the default) denies every row of this table marked degrading, which is all five, so an artifact over either limit is refused rather than shipped slower, and the diagnostic quotes the caller's own unrescued artifact. It is one predicate on the table's rows, not a test inside each rung. The same table holds the DFA-overflow rows of §3.3.3, which are degrading and outside the switch's reach: an overflow is answered by `--engine=dfa` or `-fprefilter`. A pattern that fits is byte-identical with or without the switch. Each rung's own deny flag still applies.

<a id="s8-4-p4"></a>[8.4¶4] An over-cap artifact that carries no droppable contributor, or where dropping is not enough, is refused with the figures of the smallest artifact pcrec could make without changing an answer.

<a id="s8-5"></a>
### 8.5 What a dropped rung leaves

<a id="s8-5-p1"></a>[8.5¶1] An artifact instead of a diagnostic, matching identically, with these stamps (`match_api.md` §6.3):

- <a id="s8-5-p2"></a>[8.5¶2] rung 3 fired: `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "search-filter"` where an unconstrained build reads `"unwrapped"`;
- <a id="s8-5-p3"></a>[8.5¶3] rung 4 fired: `<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE` reads `"indexed"` or `"mixed"` where it would read `"premultiplied"`;
- <a id="s8-5-p4"></a>[8.5¶4] rung 5 fired: `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none"`, `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry"` and `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY "size cap retry, hybrid N > CAP"` (the refused artifact's bytes and the cap it exceeded); apart from those the artifact is the caller's own `-fno-prefilter` one, and the rung is never taken under `-fprefilter` or on a DFA-overflow retry;
- <a id="s8-5-p5"></a>[8.5¶5] under `--engine=auto`, `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry"` where it would read `"selected"`, whenever any of rungs 2-5 fired. Under an explicit `--engine=dfa` the drop still happens (it changes an entry-point form, not the engine) and the macro reads `"forced"` without naming the retry.

<a id="s8-5-p6"></a>[8.5¶6] Each of rungs 3, 4 and 5 prints a non-fatal stderr note naming what was dropped, the cost direction and the recourse; the first reads:

```
pcrec: note: the emitted-size cap forced a smaller artifact: dropped the
optional anchored match-here machine -- loses the [OPT-2] fast path --
<prefix>_match falls back to search-and-filter, which the anchored machine
exists specifically to avoid (docs/design/anchored_match_unwrapped.md).
Raise --max-emit-bytes/--max-emit-code-bytes to keep the faster form, or
accept the fit.
```

<a id="s8-5-p7"></a>[8.5¶7] The caps are unmoved: the result is a smaller artifact, not a larger allowance. No pattern that compiled before changes by a byte, because the ladder is reached only from a refusal.

<a id="s8-5-p8"></a>[8.5¶8] A prefilter-free VM artifact whose overflow was caused by `--tune=speed` or `--tune=max-speed` raising `VM_INLINE_CHAIN_MAX_BYTES` (`tuning.md` §5) has no rung: it is refused through the recourse of §8.8.

<a id="s8-6"></a>
### 8.6 Overriding the limits

<a id="s8-6-p1"></a>[8.6¶1] `-fno-size-term` denies the unroll-ladder selection and never reaches a limit. To accept a larger artifact, raise the limit: `--max-emit-code-bytes=N` and `--max-emit-bytes=N` are raise-only (§3.3.2). The effective total cap is stamped on every artifact as `<PREFIX>_MAX_EMIT_BYTES`. The code cap, `<PREFIX>_MAX_EMIT_CODE_BYTES`, is stamped only on a VM artifact: a pure-DFA artifact has no code/table split to bound separately.

<a id="s8-6-p2"></a>[8.6¶2] `--tune=N` (`tuning.md` §5) never lowers either cap; every size-side position only tightens the size ladder's own selection (§8a, §8b).

<a id="s8-7"></a>
### 8.7 `--warn-emit-bytes=N`

<a id="s8-7-p1"></a>[8.7¶1] When an accepted artifact's total emitted bytes exceed `N`, pcrec writes one line to stderr and returns the artifact. It never refuses, changes nothing emitted, and no artifact records it:

```
pcrec: warning: large artifact: 883632 bytes of emitted C source (11418 of
code), over --warn-emit-bytes=250000. Unroll factor K=8 (default); prefilter
language n/a (no VM prefilter). See docs/spec/tuning.md for the levers, or
raise/disable the warning with --warn-emit-bytes.
```

<a id="s8-7-p2"></a>[8.7¶2] The line names the two stamps that explain the size, the unroll factor with `_UNROLL_K_WHY`'s reason and the prefilter language. The default is 250,000 total bytes (`PCREC_DEFAULT_WARN_EMIT_BYTES`); `0` disables it. It is the one size option that is not raise-only: a warning cannot fail a build, so lowering it is the intended use. For a library caller it is `pcrec_options.warn_emit_bytes`, and it is off for one who zeroes the struct rather than calling `pcrec_default_options`.

<a id="s8-8"></a>
### 8.8 Handling an oversized artifact

<a id="s8-8-p1"></a>[8.8¶1] pcrec refuses rather than emitting past either limit, and writes nothing when it refuses. The refusal is reached only after the ladder of §8.4 has failed to produce a smaller artifact. Table-dominated artifacts do not shrink with `--unroll`. The options, in the order most callers want them:

0. <a id="s8-8-p2"></a>[8.8¶2] Notice it earlier with `--warn-emit-bytes=N` (§8.7).
1. <a id="s8-8-p3"></a>[8.8¶3] Raise the limit, `--max-emit-bytes=N` or `--max-emit-code-bytes=N`. For a real build put the override in the pattern-source file's `config` block (`rxt_format.md` §1.1) so it applies per target beside the pattern; the command-line flags are for one-off compiles.
2. <a id="s8-8-p4"></a>[8.8¶4] Let the size term choose `K`, or force it: `--unroll=1` emits one body copy per counter-rung iteration and is the largest single size lever for a replication-dominated pattern. It costs a little throughput on single-level large counts and does not shrink a table- or prefilter-dominated artifact.
3. <a id="s8-8-p5"></a>[8.8¶5] Change the engine or the output: `--no-captures` and `--engine=dfa` remove the VM body; `--engine=vm` removes the hybrid DFA prefilter, most of the size when the artifact is table-dominated, at a large cost on non-matching subjects.
4. <a id="s8-8-p6"></a>[8.8¶6] Split or rewrite the pattern. Repetition counts multiply through nesting, so lowering a count inside a nest is worth far more than lowering an outer one.
5. <a id="s8-8-p7"></a>[8.8¶7] Read the stamps to see which term produced the bytes: `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K` and `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY` (`default`, `option`, `denied`, `size-model`, `size-model-declined`, `cap-rescue`, `capacity-declined`), `<PREFIX>_VM_RUNGS` for node replication, `<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE` and `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER` for the prefilter and its tables.

<a id="s8a"></a>
## 8a. `--unroll=K` and the depth an artifact reaches

<a id="s8a-p1"></a>[8a¶1] `K` is answer-identical in the language: an artifact at any `K` accepts the same strings, reports the same span and fills the same capture slots. It is not identical in the depth it reaches under the default capacities: a smaller `K` raises the per-iteration frame need, so the same `<PREFIX>_BT_FRAMES` carries a shorter subject before `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES`.

<a id="s8a-p2"></a>[8a¶2] `rx_info.subject_ceiling` is the declared bound and it moves with `K`:

| pattern | `--unroll=8` | `--unroll=1` |
|---|---|---|
| `^(a(?1)?b)$` | 512 | 341 |
| `((?1)?a)` | 512 | 341 |
| `(((?:a{0,2}b)+c){0,20}d){0,20}e` | 43 | 23 |

<a id="s8a-p3"></a>[8a¶3] Two rules follow, in opposite directions on purpose:

1. <a id="s8a-p4"></a>[8a¶4] An explicit `--unroll=K` may lower the depth the artifact reaches. That is the caller's choice, visible in the stamped `.subject_ceiling` before any subject runs; the remedies are raising the frame capacity through the options or `<PREFIX>_search_in` with a caller-supplied buffer (§5).
2. <a id="s8a-p5"></a>[8a¶5] The size term never lowers it. A `K` the compiler chooses is held to a floor: a rung whose artifact would declare less capacity than the default `K`'s, on `.frame_capacity` or `.subject_ceiling`, is not a candidate, in ordinary selection or in a cap rescue. When the `K` the term wanted is removed by the floor, the term declines and stamps `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY "capacity-declined"`.

<a id="s8b"></a>
## 8b. Three `limits.def` knees `--tune=N` moves

<a id="s8b-p1"></a>[8b¶1] A selection knee, a `limits.def` row that steers which lowering the emitter takes rather than what pcrec accepts, carries no anchor in this document (`tuning.md` §2.20). Three earn one here because `--tune=N` (`tuning.md` §5) sets each per position:

| constant | override | −2 | −1 | 0 (default) | +1 | +2 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_THRESHOLD` (bytes) | `-D` | 40,000 | 80,000 | 120,000 | — | — |
| `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_BAR` (percent) | `none` | 95 | 85 | 75 | — | — |
| `VM_INLINE_CHAIN_MAX_BYTES` (bytes) | `flag` | — | — | 4,096 | 8,192 | 8,192 |

<a id="s8b-p2"></a>[8b¶2] `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_THRESHOLD` has no CLI override, so `--tune=N` is the only per-compile lever on it. `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_BAR` has neither `-D` nor a flag, so `--tune=N` is the only lever of any kind. `VM_INLINE_CHAIN_MAX_BYTES` is overridden outright by `--vm-entry-shape=N` (`tuning.md` §2.21): an explicit spelling beats the dial.

<a id="s8b-p3"></a>[8b¶3] `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_BAR` is a percent and reads as a ceiling on the smaller `K`'s artifact: at 75 a smaller `K` ships only if its bytes are at most 75 % of the default `K`'s. A higher bar is a looser requirement, which is why the size-leaning positions raise it. The policy table that states why each cell is what it is is `tuning.md` §5.4.
